title: Efficacy Of Magnesium In Radicular Pain When Added To Local Anesthetics And Steroids In Transforaminal Epidural Injection
brief_summary: investigators want to assess the efficacy of magnesium in radicular lower limb pain when it is added to local anesthetics and steroids in the transforaminal epidural injections.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion criteria were:

* Patients of both gender.
* Patients aged from 20 up to 70 years old.
* Patients of American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status grade I and II.
* Patients admitted for pain management of their unilateral lower limb radicular pain due to lumbo-sacral disc prolapse confirmed by lumbo-sacral magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI) after failure of conservative treatments in the form of drug therapy and physiotherapy to control the pain for 6 weeks.

Exclusion criteria were:

* Patients with axial back pain without leg radiation.
* Patients with motor neurological deficits.
* Previous spine surgeries.
* Allergy to the study drugs used.
* Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus or hypertension.
* Local or systemic infection.
* Pregnancy.
* Patients with any other neurological deficits as cauda equina.
